title: Avocats du Barreau d’Aurelle announce three-day strike over aide juridictionnelle
content: The Conseil de l’ordre du barreau d’Aurelle voted on Monday evening to suspend hearings for three days from 3 November, after the Chancellerie left the *aide juridictionnelle* tariff unchanged for a fourth consecutive year. The motion passed by 214 votes to 46, with the jeunes avocats forming the bulk of the majority.

Under the current barème, an avocat assigned to a *garde à vue* receives a flat fee of 28 livres, and a first-instance hearing is remunerated at 96 livres — figures the barreau says have fallen by a third in real terms since 2019. The ministry points to an enveloppe of nine million livres reserved for legal aid in the coming budget and to promised *concertations* in January.

The strike will not affect *urgences*: gardes à vue, comparutions immédiates and detention hearings remain covered by a minimum service. Several chambers of the tribunal judiciaire have already postponed their *rôles* for the first week of November, and the bâtonnier has asked the Chancellerie to reopen negotiations before the *rentrée* of the courts.
author: Jeanne Vasseur, correspondante judiciaire — Agence des Républiques (ADR)
